note: Text is as checked (served text, including round-4 rationales on ITSUP chapter checks). Excludes the 40 round-1 ids (ROUND1_IDS) and the 180 ids in spot-check-round2/3/4-sample.json. No item text was changed by this round. This file is the record of what was checked.

items.text: Lab ticket-intake sentence: half the quarterdeck badges failed after lunch, reader warm. Commands?
options: classify request, impact 1, escalate no
Open the reader panel first
classify incident, impact many, escalate yes
classify break-fix, impact 1, escalate no
items.correct: classify incident, impact many, escalate yes
items.explanation: Half the quarterdeck badges failed and the reader is warm: many people are affected and there is heat on access-control hardware, so the lab answer is classify incident, impact many, escalate yes. “Request, impact 1” treats a failure as a new ask, “break-fix, impact 1” understates both the scope and the heat, and opening the reader panel is the unsafe move the lab fails on. See 1.5. Source: Course lab ticket-intake (lesson 1.5 command list); ITIL 4 Incident management (impact and escalation).

items.text: An unknown caller wants a password reset right now. What do you do first?
options: Verify identity per shop policy
Reset it and sort identity later
Disable the firewall
Share the admin password
items.correct: Verify identity per shop policy
items.explanation: A password reset hands the account to whoever asked, so the caller’s identity has to be verified under shop policy before anything changes. “Reset it and sort identity later” is exactly what a social engineer counts on: urgency is pressure, not proof of identity. See 1.1 / 1.4.

items.text: A PCIe 4.0 x16 GPU is installed in a mechanical x16 slot that is electrically only x4 on a small board. What performance outcome should you expect?
options: It falls back to PCIe 1.0 speed
It works, with less bandwidth than an electrical x16 slot
It will not POST because the lane counts differ
It runs at full x16 speed because the slot is physically x16
items.correct: It works, with less bandwidth than an electrical x16 slot
items.explanation: PCIe negotiates the lane count, so the card works but has a quarter of the bandwidth of an electrical x16 slot.

items.text: Secure Boot in one sentence a user will accept:
options: It makes the system disk faster
It replaces antivirus software
It encrypts the system drive against theft
Firmware starts only a signed bootloader
items.correct: Firmware starts only a signed bootloader
items.explanation: Secure Boot means the firmware will start only a bootloader whose signature it trusts. That blocks some bootkits, and it is also why an unsigned shop USB stick will not start. It does not make the disk faster, it does not replace antivirus once Windows is running, and it does not encrypt anything: drive encryption is BitLocker’s job. See 2.2. Source: UEFI Specification 2.10, Secure Boot and Driver Signing; Microsoft Learn, "Secure boot" and "BitLocker overview".

items.text: Debug LED reads MEM, long beeps, no video. POST command?
options: post power
post memory
post ok
post display
items.correct: post memory
items.explanation: The debug LED reads MEM and the board gives long beeps, and both point at memory during POST, so the lab command is post memory. No video is a consequence: the board stops before it ever sends a picture, so post display chases the screen the LED has already ruled out. post power fits a board with no fans and no LEDs, which is not this one, and post ok would mean POST passed. See 2.5. Source: Course hw-board bench card (lesson 2.5 POST table); motherboard vendor manuals (DRAM/MEM debug LED marks a memory fault during POST).

items.text: Settings shows 8 GB RAM, but two 8 GB modules are installed. What is the most likely cause?
options: One module is not seated or not detected
Windows always reserves half the RAM
The CPU only supports 8 GB
The page file is too small
items.correct: One module is not seated or not detected
items.explanation: A mismatch between installed and reported memory points to seating, compatibility or a failed module.

items.text: A parts list shows “M.2 2280 NVMe”. What does 2280 tell you?
options: The drive’s capacity is 2,280 gigabytes
The drive uses PCIe generation 2.2
The drive reads at 2,280 megabytes per second
The card is 22 mm wide and 80 mm long
items.correct: The card is 22 mm wide and 80 mm long
items.explanation: M.2 size codes give width and length in millimetres; 2280 is 22 × 80 mm.

items.text: Four 4 TB disks are configured as RAID 5. What is the usable capacity?
options: 16 TB
8 TB
12 TB
4 TB
items.correct: 12 TB
items.explanation: RAID 5 uses one disk’s worth of space for parity: (4 − 1) × 4 TB = 12 TB.

items.text: A NAS must ride through short outages and shut down cleanly in long ones. What should be installed?
options: A UPS that signals the NAS to shut down
A surge protector with a high joule rating
A larger power supply inside the NAS
A second NAS that mirrors the first one
items.correct: A UPS that signals the NAS to shut down
items.explanation: Only a UPS supplies power during an outage, and its signal lets the NAS shut down before the battery runs out.

items.text: A 65 W brick on a chassis that expects 130 W often looks like:
options: Better thermals under load
A faster CPU boost clock
Slow charging or CPU throttling
A failing SSD or file corruption
items.correct: Slow charging or CPU throttling
items.explanation: An adapter rated well below what the laptop expects cannot supply full power, so the laptop charges slowly or not at all under load and throttles the CPU. It does not improve thermals or boost clocks, and it does not damage files. Read both labels. See 4.1.

items.text: Mail works on cellular, fails on building Wi-Fi. Factory reset the phone?
options: Yes to remove the work profile
No. Isolate the WLAN / portal / proxy
Yes always
Yes, if MDM is installed on the phone
items.correct: No. Isolate the WLAN / portal / proxy
items.explanation: Mail works on cellular, so the phone, its radio and the mail account all work; only the building Wi-Fi path fails, so isolate that path (WLAN, captive portal, proxy). A factory reset, “always” or otherwise, wipes the device and still would not fix the building network. Removing the work profile is the MDM owner’s decision, not a hallway fix, and having MDM installed is a reason not to reset, not a reason to. See 4.2. Source: Microsoft Learn, Intune "Remove devices by using wipe, retire, or manually unenrolling the device"; course 4.2 isolation table.

items.text: Print path order?
options: Printer panel → app → spooler → port → cable
App → spooler → driver/port → link → device
Device → cable → app → driver only
Driver only — reinstall it every time
items.correct: App → spooler → driver/port → link → device
items.explanation: A print job travels application → Windows print system (spooler and queue) → driver and port → link (USB or network) → device, and you isolate along that path by scope. Starting at the printer panel, or jumping from device and cable back to the app, scrambles the order so you cannot tell which box failed, and “reinstall the driver every time” is a reflex that tests only one box. See 4.3. Source: Microsoft Support, "Fix printer connection and printing problems in Windows"; Microsoft Learn, Print Spooler service; course 4.3.

items.text: How many usable host addresses does a /27 IPv4 subnet provide?
items.explanation: A /27 has 32 addresses; the network and broadcast addresses leave 30 usable.

items.text: Which DNS record type identifies the mail servers for a domain?
options: PTR record
CNAME record
AAAA record
MX record
items.correct: MX record
items.explanation: MX records list a domain’s mail servers; PTR is reverse lookup and CNAME is an alias.

items.text: Which change most improves a new SOHO router’s security?
options: Hide the SSID broadcast on the router
Turn on MAC address filtering
Change the default admin password
Move the router to channel 6
items.correct: Change the default admin password
items.explanation: Default credentials are the biggest hole; hiding the SSID and MAC filtering are not security controls.

items.text: A snapshot is:
options: A restore point for trying a change, not a backup
A backup copy stored in another building
A RAID 5 array spread across the host
A full off-site copy of the guest disk, kept for years
items.correct: A restore point for trying a change, not a backup
items.explanation: A snapshot records a VM’s state so you can roll back a change; it depends on the original virtual disk and usually lives on the same storage. That is why it is not a backup: if that storage fails, the snapshot is lost with it. A real backup copy is stored separately, ideally off-site. See 6.3.

items.text: A company uses a hosted email service and manages only users and settings. Which model is this?
options: SaaS
IaaS
PaaS
On-premises
items.correct: SaaS
items.explanation: With SaaS the provider runs the application; the customer manages its users, data and configuration.

items.text: Correct process order starts with:
options: Identify who, what, how many, safety
Reimage the PC to start clean
Flush DNS and then close the ticket
Disable Defender and retest
items.correct: Identify who, what, how many, safety
items.explanation: The process starts with identify: who is affected, what outcome is missing, how many people and whether there is a safety stop. Without that you cannot form a theory worth testing. Reimaging, flushing DNS and disabling Defender are changes made before anyone knows what the problem is, and closing the ticket after a flush skips verification. The user saying “it’s DNS” is not identification. See 7.1. Source: CompTIA A+ 220-1201 exam objectives, troubleshooting methodology section, step 1 (identify the problem) (a competency standard, not a tested objective in the 220-1200 series).

items.text: Verified means:
options: You left the user a voicemail
The outcome the user called about works
Task Manager looks calm again on the PC
The SLA timer has expired
items.correct: The outcome the user called about works
items.explanation: Verified means the outcome the user called about works again, confirmed by re-running the test that failed, with the user. A voicemail is a message, not a confirmation. A calm Task Manager is supporting evidence about one machine, not the user’s outcome, and an expired SLA timer measures time, not whether anything was fixed. Closing a ticket is not the same as fixing it. See 7.3 / 1.1. Source: CompTIA A+ 220-1201 exam objectives, troubleshooting methodology section, step 5 (verify full system functionality) (a competency standard, not a tested objective in the 220-1200 series); ITIL 4 Incident management (closure confirmed with the user).

items.text: Which escalation lets the next tier start without repeating your work?
options: “User still cannot connect, we tried everything here”
“Urgent — please call the user back today”
Impact, scope, evidence, actions tried and the request
“Same as last week’s ticket, see that one”
items.correct: Impact, scope, evidence, actions tried and the request
items.explanation: A structured package carries the evidence forward so tier 2 can begin at the test step.

items.text: A Windows 11 Pro version is past its 24-month servicing period. What is the main risk?
options: It will stop booting at the next restart
Its Pro licence turns into a Home licence
It no longer gets security updates
Its user accounts are deleted automatically
items.correct: It no longer gets security updates
items.explanation: Out-of-service versions stop receiving security updates; Home and Pro are serviced for 24 months, Enterprise and Education for 36.

items.text: May you turn the firewall profile off for a game launcher?
options: No
Yes
Yes, if the user is an administrator
Yes, after taking a snapshot
items.correct: No
items.explanation: The firewall profile stays on. Turning it off for a game launcher removes protection for the whole device; an approved rule or exception is the owner’s decision. Admin rights or a snapshot do not make it acceptable. See 8.3 / 5.2 / 1.4.

items.text: A PC crashes daily since a driver was installed on Tuesday. Which WinRE option undoes it but keeps personal files?
options: Reset this PC with the Remove everything choice
Command Prompt with format C: /q
System Restore to a point before Tuesday
A clean install from a recovery drive
items.correct: System Restore to a point before Tuesday
items.explanation: System Restore rolls back drivers, settings and system files to the restore point while keeping personal files.

items.text: Domain sign-in fails with a Kerberos error and the laptop clock is 9 minutes fast. What is the likely cause?
options: An expired Windows licence on the laptop itself
Clock skew beyond the default 5-minute limit
A full recycle bin on the system drive
A missing printer driver for the device
items.correct: Clock skew beyond the default 5-minute limit
items.explanation: Kerberos rejects authentication when clocks differ by more than the tolerance, 5 minutes by default.

items.text: A file shows -rw-r----- in ls -l. What can members of the file’s group do?
options: Read the file but not change it
Read, change and execute the file
Nothing, because only the owner has rights
Execute it as a program but not read it
items.correct: Read the file but not change it
items.explanation: The middle triplet r-- gives the group read only; the owner has rw-, others ---.

items.text: A managed Mac must get a configuration profile and app. What is the supported way to deliver them?
options: Emailing the profile to the user
Signing in with the technician’s Apple Account
Disabling System Integrity Protection
Through the organisation’s MDM
items.correct: Through the organisation’s MDM
items.explanation: MDM delivers profiles and apps under policy; personal workarounds bypass management and auditing.

items.text: A Mac user gets “access denied” on a share that colleagues in the same group can open. What do you check first?
options: The user’s group membership and share permissions
The Mac’s network cable
The macOS version
The file server’s disk space
items.correct: The user’s group membership and share permissions
items.explanation: An access-denied message is an entitlement answer: the network path worked.

items.text: How does a Mac user connect to the Windows share \\files\budget?
options: System Settings → Network → Add Server → files/budget
Finder → Go → Connect to Server → smb://files/budget
Terminal: ping files, then open the result list
Disk Utility → File → New Image → files/budget
items.correct: Finder → Go → Connect to Server → smb://files/budget
items.explanation: macOS connects to SMB shares with smb:// URLs from Finder’s Connect to Server.

items.text: Why should a technician not reimage a ransomware-infected PC before security reviews it?
options: Reimaging spreads the ransomware to backups
The licence key is erased by reimaging
Reimaging takes longer than paying the ransom
The evidence of how it got in would be lost
items.correct: The evidence of how it got in would be lost
items.explanation: Security needs the device’s state to find the entry point and other affected systems.

items.text: Decommissioning drives from a finance PC requires which disposal standard mindset?
options: Cryptographic erase or physical destruction per policy
A quick format
Deleting the user profiles
Reset this PC with “Keep my files”
items.correct: Cryptographic erase or physical destruction per policy
items.explanation: A quick format leaves data recoverable; use cryptographic erase or physical destruction per policy.

items.text: Under RFC 3227, which evidence should be collected first?
options: The contents of the system disk
Archived backup tapes
Memory and the process table
Remote syslog records
items.correct: Memory and the process table
items.explanation: Collect from most to least volatile; memory and process data disappear at power-off.

items.text: An app fails; ping to the server IP works; ping to its name fails. Which fault domain?
options: Failing disk
Battery
DNS domain
Office installation
items.correct: DNS domain
items.explanation: Pinging the server’s IP proves the network path; failing by name points to DNS. A failing disk, the battery or the Office installation would not explain IP working while the name fails. See 11.2 / 5.3.

items.text: Clean image because one app crashes?
options: Yes, if the user is on a Mac
Yes, if the app is SaaS
No. Isolate the app first
Yes, a reimage is quicker
items.correct: No. Isolate the app first
items.explanation: One crashing app is isolated first: repair or reset it, or try another profile. A clean image throws away the evidence and the user’s setup for a problem that may be in one app, whatever the platform or delivery. See 11.3.

items.text: After 45 minutes you have found several unrelated faults and unknown installs. What is usually best?
options: Plan a rebuild with a verified backup and app list
Keep repairing until each of the faults is fixed in turn
Disable the antivirus to rule it out fully
Close the ticket and ask the user to retry
items.correct: Plan a rebuild with a verified backup and app list
items.explanation: Several unrelated faults and unknown changes past the time box favour a planned rebuild.

items.text: A Store app crashes on launch. Which option fixes its files but keeps its data?
options: Uninstalling and reinstalling the app
Repair, in the app’s Advanced options
Reset, in the app’s Advanced options
Network reset, in Settings
items.correct: Repair, in the app’s Advanced options
items.explanation: For Store and many built-in apps, Settings → Apps → Installed apps → Advanced options offers Repair (fixes the app; its data is not affected) and Reset (also deletes the app’s data on this device). Reinstalling removes local data too.

items.text: A change window is 02:00–04:00. At 03:50 a risky step remains. Best decision framework?
options: Disable monitoring to avoid alerts
Stop and roll back per the plan
Continue, because it is nearly done
Skip the remaining tests
items.correct: Stop and roll back per the plan
items.explanation: The plan’s go/no-go rule applies: stop and roll back rather than overrun into business hours without approval.

items.text: A friend in another department asks you to look up a colleague’s phone number in the HR system. What is appropriate?
options: Ask HR to send it to your friend
Give the friend your login
Decline: you may access data only for your job
Look it up quickly
items.correct: Decline: you may access data only for your job
items.explanation: Access to personal data is limited to job need; sharing credentials is never allowed.

items.text: Backups run once a night. The data owner requires an RPO of one hour. What is true?
options: The plan meets the RPO easily
RPO only applies to databases
The RTO decides this, not RPO
The plan cannot meet the RPO
items.correct: The plan cannot meet the RPO
items.explanation: A nightly schedule can lose up to 24 hours of data, far more than a one-hour RPO allows.

items.text: A working laptop moves from the reception desk to the spares cupboard. What changes in its asset record?
options: Status and location (spare, in stores), with the ticket linked
A new asset tag is issued, because the device now has a new home
Nothing changes until the laptop is finally disposed of
Its serial number is updated to match the new location
items.correct: Status and location (spare, in stores), with the ticket linked
items.explanation: An asset record tracks a device through its life: status (in use, in repair, spare, disposed) and location/owner change when it moves, with the ticket linked. The tag and serial stay the same; disposal is a different status.

items.text: ipconfig /all shows IPv4 169.254.31.8 and a blank default gateway. What does this indicate?
options: The DNS server has returned a wrong name
The adapter has no physical link at all
No DHCP server answered the adapter
A static address was typed in by hand
items.correct: No DHCP server answered the adapter
items.explanation: A 169.254 address is APIPA, self-assigned when DHCP fails; a missing link would show Media disconnected.

items.text: nslookup returns the right address, but the browser goes to the wrong server. What should you check next?
options: The DHCP lease time on the router
The speed and duplex setting of the adapter
The Windows Update history page
The hosts file and the local DNS cache
items.correct: The hosts file and the local DNS cache
items.explanation: nslookup asks the DNS server directly; the Windows resolver also uses the cache and hosts file, so a difference points there.

items.text: Settings paths gym includes:
options: About, Ethernet, Update, Accounts, Services
PSU internals, fan headers, CMOS
Hyper-V delete-all, snapshots, vSwitch, uplinks
Printer firmware, toner, drum
items.correct: About, Ethernet, Update, Accounts, Services
items.explanation: The settings-paths lab drills the Windows views used as evidence: About, Ethernet, Update, Accounts and Services. PSU internals, deleting Hyper-V snapshots and printer firmware are outside it, or unsafe. See 13.5.

items.text: A laptop shows a 169.254.x.x address after a cable move. Which is the least disruptive first step?
options: ipconfig /release, then ipconfig /renew
netsh winsock reset, then restart
Settings → Network & internet → Network reset
Reinstall the network adapter driver
items.correct: ipconfig /release, then ipconfig /renew
items.explanation: Climb the reset ladder one rung at a time: renewing the lease (rung 1) only drops and re-requests the DHCP address. A stack reset, a full network reset and a driver reinstall undo far more configuration.

items.text: A /64 is the common host subnet size for which protocol family?
options: IPv6
IPv4 private networks
IPv4 public networks
Multicast groups only
items.correct: IPv6
items.explanation: IPv6 LAN subnets are /64 so SLAAC can form interface identifiers.

items.text: Users report the whole floor slowed to a halt after someone patched a cable between two wall jacks. Most likely cause?
options: A layer-2 loop causing a broadcast storm
A duplex mismatch on one of the access ports
A DHCP scope running out
A DNS server failure
items.correct: A layer-2 loop causing a broadcast storm
items.explanation: Two jacks on the same switch form a loop; without STP edge protection (BPDU Guard) broadcasts multiply.

items.text: Two switches are trunked, but VLAN 30 hosts on each switch cannot reach each other. Other VLANs work. What do you check first?
options: The PoE budget on both switches
The DNS records for VLAN 30
Whether VLAN 30 is allowed on the trunk
The spanning-tree root bridge priority
items.correct: Whether VLAN 30 is allowed on the trunk
items.explanation: If one VLAN fails across a working trunk, it is usually missing from the allowed list (or not created on one switch).

items.text: Which tool finds which switch port a wall jack is patched to, without a live network?
options: Loopback plug
Spectrum analyser
Toner and probe
Optical power meter
items.correct: Toner and probe
items.explanation: A tone generator on the jack and a probe at the patch panel identify the cable without powering anything.

items.text: Anycast DNS is used so that?
options: Each client gets its own server address
Several sites advertise one address and clients reach the nearest
One server answers every client worldwide
Clients rotate through server addresses
items.correct: Several sites advertise one address and clients reach the nearest
items.explanation: Several sites advertise the same address; routing delivers each client to the topologically nearest one.

items.text: A branch circuit drops every afternoon. What should you collect before calling the provider?
options: The router’s serial number only
Timestamps, interface errors and your test results
The provider’s list of other customers
A screenshot of one speed test from your own laptop
items.correct: Timestamps, interface errors and your test results
items.explanation: Providers act on evidence: when it happened, what the interface counters showed, and tests that isolate your side.

items.text: Which 2.4 GHz channels do not overlap in most regions?
options: 1, 2 and 3
items.explanation: In 20 MHz widths, channels 1, 6 and 11 are the non-overlapping set used in North America and most designs.

items.text: Clients on a new VLAN get 169.254 addresses. The DHCP server is on another subnet. What is most likely missing?
options: A NAT rule for the VLAN
A static route to the DHCP server on each client
A DHCP relay (helper address) on the VLAN gateway
A DNS A record for the server
items.correct: A DHCP relay (helper address) on the VLAN gateway
items.explanation: Discover is a broadcast and does not cross routers; the gateway must relay it to the server.

items.text: A web server’s address changed, but some users still reach the old IP. What explains it?
options: A missing MX record
An expired DHCP lease
A wrong subnet mask configured on the web server
Cached records that have not reached their TTL
items.correct: Cached records that have not reached their TTL
items.explanation: Resolvers and clients cache answers for the record’s TTL; lower the TTL before planned changes.

items.text: NAT hides internal addresses from the public Internet. Which tradeoff is most associated with basic many-to-one NAT?
options: Outbound web browsing stops working
Internal hosts cannot reach each other
The ISP must resolve DNS
Inbound connections need explicit port mappings
items.correct: Inbound connections need explicit port mappings
items.explanation: PAT tracks outbound flows automatically; unsolicited inbound connections need explicit port mappings.

items.text: Latency is low but jitter is high on a voice VLAN. Impact?
options: Voice degrades despite low average delay
Email delivery fails for some users
DHCP leases expire earlier than set
Calls cannot connect at all
items.correct: Voice degrades despite low average delay
items.explanation: Voice needs steady delay; high jitter causes choppy audio even when average latency is fine.

items.text: Management plane protection on network devices should include?
options: HTTP management with a login banner
AAA, SSH/HTTPS, management ACLs and logging
Telnet with a shared password
SNMPv1 with community “public” read-write
items.correct: AAA, SSH/HTTPS, management ACLs and logging
items.explanation: AAA, encrypted management (SSH/HTTPS), management ACLs and central logging.

items.text: Which technology segments east-west traffic in a data center at scale more flexibly than only VLANs?
options: More VLANs on a single trunk
Larger, flatter subnets
Overlay segmentation (e.g., VXLAN) with policy
More Spanning Tree instances
items.correct: Overlay segmentation (e.g., VXLAN) with policy
items.explanation: Overlays such as VXLAN (with policy) scale segmentation beyond the VLAN ID space and across a routed fabric.

items.text: One user cannot reach a single website; everyone else can. Most likely scope?
options: The user’s device or account
The core switch
The ISP circuit
The data-centre firewall rules
items.correct: The user’s device or account
items.explanation: A single user and single destination failing while others succeed points to the client (proxy, DNS cache, hosts file, browser).

items.text: A change caused an outage and the fix is unclear. What does a good change plan already contain?
options: The vendor’s support phone number only
A tested rollback procedure
A list of users to blame
Only the new configuration
items.correct: A tested rollback procedure
items.explanation: Rollback is planned before the change so service can be restored quickly.

items.text: You changed a trunk’s allowed VLANs to fix an outage. Which document must be updated?
options: The user’s password list
The DHCP lease table
The printer inventory
The network diagram and configuration record
items.correct: The network diagram and configuration record
items.explanation: Documentation must match the running network or the next incident starts from wrong information.

items.text: Which interface commands make a port an access port in VLAN 20?
options: vlan 20, then name ACCESS
switchport mode access, then switchport access vlan 20
switchport mode trunk, then switchport trunk native vlan 20
items.correct: switchport mode access, then switchport access vlan 20
items.explanation: Access mode plus the access VLAN assigns the port; the vlan command alone only creates the VLAN.
